details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh:~75 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The `PR comment audit:` stop condition is case-sensitive, so a prompt heading casing change can prevent the extractor from stopping at the right section.
  WHY: If the sentinel never matches, later section text reaches the arithmetic parser and can trigger a false gate-B failure.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:~40-115 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The local fallback definitions for `_embed_input_file` and prompt-budget helpers are unreachable because `gh_helpers.sh` already defines the same functions.
  WHY: Any fix made in that dead block will never run, leaving the real code path unchanged.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~13100 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The editor-summary selector can pick a comment that merely starts with `AI autofix editor summary` rather than the real summary comment.
  WHY: The audit validator then runs on the wrong body and fails the gate for the wrong reason.
- scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh:67-74 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The audit-field extraction regex can misparse malformed lines that contain unexpected numbers.
  WHY: A malformed line can yield the wrong counts and either trip a false mismatch or mask a real one.
- scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh:83 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The unparseable-line warning omits PR/context details.
  WHY: Operators cannot easily correlate the warning to a specific PR in multi-PR poll cycles.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2216-2222 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: `_integration_branch_ahead_of_default` can fail the compare API path without emitting a numeric result that callers expect.
  WHY: Callers that treat an empty result as `0` may falsely consider the branch in sync while the API is failing.
- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py:1735 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The initial jittered backoff is very short.
  WHY: The first retry can still collide under concurrent writers, leading to repeated push conflicts.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1360-1372 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The nonce trailer lacks a clear end-of-input marker.
  WHY: Some tokenizers may include the nonce in semantic parsing and subtly affect model behavior across retries.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:13018-13148 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: Gate B does not verify that the audit entries correspond to the current PR head SHA.
  WHY: A push that lands between sampling and validation can make the force-merge decision use stale audit data.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:13054-13058 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The fresh comment refetch before Gate B is not paired with a refresh of the earlier PR metadata.
  WHY: The PR can change state between the two reads and still be judged against stale Gate-A mergeability data.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:13065 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: `mktemp` failure can leave the noop-summary temp path unusable but the script continues until a later write check.
  WHY: This turns an early environment problem into a later ERROR alert instead of failing fast.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:1718-1724 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: A future-dated `head_pushed_at` can push the effective anchor into the future.
  WHY: Stall detection can be suppressed indefinitely until wall-clock time catches up.
- scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh:106-110 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: Removing the `total=0` bypass makes zero-issue summaries subject to the normal arithmetic check.
  WHY: That can turn legitimate zero-count edge cases into false mismatches.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:4045-4046 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: `EDITOR_NOOP_REFUSAL` is exported, but the merge logic still gates only on `EDITOR_NOOP_SUSPICIOUS`.
  WHY: A refusal can be treated like an ordinary suspicious no-op and still proceed through the same force-merge path.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:9563,9579 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: `CWS_AHEAD_BY` is propagated as an empty string instead of being omitted on API failure.
  WHY: The downstream Python argument handling can distinguish `""` from missing and mis-handle ahead-by validation.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~12875-12930 | severity=medium | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The retry-threshold count and the Gate B audit validation are computed from different comment snapshots.
  WHY: A new editor summary can land between them, so the count and validation can refer to different summaries.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:~1671-1683 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The refusal short-circuit leaves `tmp_err` behind.
  WHY: Repeated refusal-triggered retries leak temp files in `${TMPDIR}` and can eventually fill the runner disk.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:~376-410 | severity=medium | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: Capturing the full PR diff into a shell variable can silently truncate very large diffs before UTF-8-safe capping runs.
  WHY: The judge can receive a corrupted or partial prompt without knowing it.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~5829-5893 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The orchestrator-managed in-flight-review guard duplicates the complex jq filter instead of factoring through the existing helper path.
  WHY: Any future drift in the workflow-name or timestamp logic can make this path disagree with the rest of the review-run detection code.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~7693-7776 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The standalone retrigger path duplicates the same in-flight-review jq filter as the orchestrator-managed path.
  WHY: A future fix applied to only one copy will create asymmetric behavior between the two stall-recovery paths.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~7710 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The in-flight-review skip path returns early without marking the stall counter for later escalation.
  WHY: A PR that keeps an in-flight review run can stay suppressed forever instead of escalating to the stall judge.
- scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh:42-50 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new `real_audit` filter strips `editor failed` lines, but the fallback summary writer emits that phrase in the runtime-failure path.
  WHY: The producer and validator can disagree about whether an audit section is real or fallback, breaking the gate contract.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_noop_suspicious_recovery.py:entire file | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new test file reimplements a large poller harness and hard-codes several runtime literals.
  WHY: It can drift from production behavior while still passing, reducing its ability to catch contract regressions.
- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py:1734 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Jitter is only applied to the push retry, not the preceding fetch/rebase critical section.
  WHY: Two concurrent writers can still race all the way to push and overwrite each other’s memory record.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:multiple | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new refusal strings and env var were added without a compatibility shim for the old names and grep-based contracts.
  WHY: Existing dashboards and downstream consumers that key on the old literals will not observe the new refusal path.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
